duel.summary: Fixed all 11 findings inside the owned paths (not committed, per the worker instructions). (1) Throw chord window: rules.throwChordFrames = 2. A light or heavy that a free fighter started becomes the throw when the partner button arrives within 2 frames, before the first active frame. The throw keeps the frames already spent, so J/K at 0, 1 or 2 frames apart all grab on frame 13, and a lone jab is still 7 frames. The validator rejects a window that reaches any light or heavy startup. (2) A throw is cancelled only by a strike contact (hit or block) on that frame; strikeActive was removed. (3) separate() breaks an exact tie by start-of-frame x, then velocity, then facing, and a full tie stays put; a new mirrored symmetry test covers it and fails on the old rule. (4) movesetVersion(moveset) is the data's FNV-1a-64 canonical hash (equal to hashState, memoised per object). MOVESET_VERSION = 248675b2a680c2c7, and the hand-written version field was removed from DuelMoveset. (5) restoreDuel validates every field (exact keys, types, integer ranges, known actions and move ids, events, result, attack/moveId and over/result consistency). (6) The Duel* types are z.infer of their schemas, the timing is narrowed by a transform over moveTimingSchema, and a typed both() helper replaces the three Pair casts. (7) The symmetry test asserts the frame-28 jab trade. (8, 10) docs/duel.md covers the chord window and counter-slash invulnerability, and the opening-hit check adds advance * (startup + active). (9, 11) A guard break adds 30 stamina, capped, with tests for the cap and for regeneration timing. Determinism fixture: the one-input change is now a first-frame thrust, because the re-timed log absorbs the old first-frame dash by frame 2069 (pushbox pinning in the corner); the version pin was updated. Checks run here, all exit 0: npm ci; npm run typecheck; npm run test:unit (222 passed); npm run test:integration (14 passed); npm run build (both postbuild self-checks and the build smoke passed).
open_assumptions: A converted throw keeps the light or heavy's elapsed frames, so it is active when a simultaneous J+K would be. It does not restart its 12-frame startup from the second press.
DuelMoveset no longer has a version field. Consumers (duel-online) use movesetVersion(moveset) or state.movesetVersion.
movesetVersion memoises by object identity (a WeakMap), which assumes moveset objects are never mutated in place. A changed moveset must be a new object.
Fighters that tie on x, start-of-frame x, velocity and facing are left overlapping for that frame, because no rule that ignores the slot can pick a side for them.

findings.message: packages/content/src/moves/version.ts memoises movesetVersion per moveset object in a WeakMap, while the z.infer-derived DuelMoveset/DuelRules/DuelArena/DuelFighter/DuelMove/Box types in schema.ts lost the readonly modifiers the hand-written interfaces had (only the moves and comboScaling arrays got .readonly()). An in-place mutation such as `config.moveset.rules.maxHealth = 2` or `duelistMoveset.moves[0].damage = 99` now type-checks and keeps the stale memoised version, so stepDuel/restoreDuel/replayDuel would accept states and logs from the old data. Restore readonly on the inferred types (or deep-freeze the exported moveset) so the memo's immutability assumption is enforced rather than documented only as an open assumption.
findings.requirement: Derive the version that snapshots and replays carry from the move data itself (for example `hashState` of the moveset), so changed data can never keep an old version.

findings.message: The moveset validator (schema.ts, THROW_CHORD_PARTNER loop) checks throwChordFrames only against the light/heavy moves' startups, not against the throw's own startup. chordThrow (step.ts:343) converts after detection and sets actionFrame to start-of-frame actionFrame + 1, so with a throw whose startup is <= throwChordFrames the converted throw's active move frame on the conversion frame is never checked for a grab (it could whiff entirely with 1 active frame). Not reachable with the Duelist data (throw startup 12), but the validator should also require throwChordFrames < the throw's startup.
findings.requirement: Add a short throw chord window (one or two frames, a named rule constant): a light or heavy that a free fighter started converts into a throw when its partner button arrives within the window, before the move's first active frame.

findings.message: separate()/leftFirst (step.ts:440-477) returns the fighters unchanged on a full tie (equal x, start-of-frame x, vx and facing), leaving pushboxes overlapping, possibly for several frames while both stay idle. This is forced by slot-neutrality and is documented in docs/duel.md and the worker's assumptions, but the duelFighterSchema pushbox comment in schema.ts still states 'Two fighters' pushboxes never overlap'; qualify it.
findings.requirement: `separate()` breaks an exact tie (equal x and equal facing) by slot, so a mirrored run can differ. Break it without reference to the slot (for example by previous x or velocity), and cover it with the symmetry test.

findings.message: restoreDuel range coverage is partial (packages/simulation/src/duel/determinism.test.ts, 'restoring a snapshot'). The leaf sweep checks every field for a wrong type or a missing value, and the it.each table checks some ranges: x at both walls, fractional y, health, stamina above max, facing, action, fighter moveId, combo, held, buffer above max, frame, phase, rng, event kind/attacker, extra fields, and consistency. Several bounds that snapshot.ts enforces have no test: negative y, stamina, staminaIdle, actionFrame, timer and buffer values; an unknown move id string in an event (only fighters.moveId is covered); negative event damage; and result.winner, result.reason and result.frame out of range (these get only the type sweep). Removing any of those checks from duelStateCheck would still pass the suite. Add range cases for them, at least an unknown event moveId, since 'known move ids' is named in the requirement.
findings.requirement: Validate every field of a restored state (types, integer ranges, known move ids, both fighters) before it is stepped, and refuse anything else.

inputs.decisions:
# Decisions: duel-core-fixes

From the operator session of 2026-09-24, written by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction to finish slices 1 and 2. The findings come from the assistant's review of duel-core-001's diff (both P1s, which the official reviewers missed) and from the official general and coverage reviews of that run.

## Decisions

- This is a follow-up feature on top of duel-core-001's result, not a new run of `duel-core`: the lane changes only what `duel-task.md` lists, and reviewers review this diff.
- Throw input: a light or heavy started by a free fighter converts into a throw when the other button arrives within a short chord window (one or two frames, a named rule constant), so a keyboard J+K with ordinary rollover becomes a throw. Conversion is preferred over delaying a lone button because it keeps §8's startups (jab 7 frames) intact. §8 asks for keyboard rollover to be checked.
- A throw is cancelled only by a strike that hits or is blocked on the same frame, never by an active hitbox that misses.
- A guard break adds 30 stamina, capped at the maximum: the plain reading of §7's "restores 30 stamina" (duel-core-001 set it to 30).
- The moveset version is derived from the move data (a hash), not written by hand.
- One lane (`duel`) with the same owned paths as `duel-core`, so it can still run beside `world-sea`.

## Assumptions

- The replay fixtures and hash pins change because input timing changes; that is expected and documented.
- The chord window applies only to a fighter that can act; the existing 4-frame buffer still covers inputs made during recovery.

## Deferred

- Haki, fruit kits and the other duel-core deferrals stand.
- Adding the new subpath exports to `scripts/smoke-build.ts`: done when `world-sea` (which owns `scripts/`) is merged.

concerns.message: Finding 4 suggests `hashState` of the moveset, but `content` cannot import `simulation`, and `packages/simulation/src/hash.ts` is outside the owned paths. Content's `postbuild` also requires `MOVESET_VERSION` to be exported from `content/moves`. The bigger trap is keeping `version` as a stored field of `DuelMoveset` that `stepDuel`, `restoreDuel` and `replayDuel` trust (step.ts:55, snapshot.ts:19, replay.ts:46). Tests and callers build movesets by spreading (determinism.test.ts:119), and `{...duelistMoveset, rules: {...}}` keeps the old version with new data. The hash also has to exclude the `version` field itself, or it would be circular.
concerns.consequence: The finding's aim (changed data can never keep an old version) quietly fails. A snapshot or replay taken on the old data is accepted by a config with changed data, unless the acceptance test happens to rebuild the version field by hand. Reviewers would then send it back. Recomputing the hash naively on every `stepDuel` call means canonicalize plus a BigInt FNV over several KB, 3,600 times per trace. That slows the unit suite noticeably and eats into §19's 8 ms step budget.

concerns.message: Validating every field in `restoreDuel` (finding 5) invites adding `zod` to `packages/simulation/package.json`, which has no zod today. The root `package-lock.json` records each workspace's dependencies and is outside the owned paths. Separately, checking only each field's type and range misses cross-field invariants the step depends on: `action === "attack"` if and only if `moveId` is a known id; `actionFrame` and `timer` within the move's duration; buffer values ≤ `inputBufferFrames`; `held` within `DUEL_INPUT_MASK`; x within the walls; a result present if and only if the phase is `over`.
concerns.consequence: Adding zod leaves `package-lock.json` out of sync, so `npm ci` fails and the lane stops as `blocked` (a check that passes only by changing a path outside the owned paths). If only per-field checks are done, a snapshot with `action: "attack", moveId: null` passes the restore and then throws inside `progress()` (`findMove(moveset, null)`), which breaks the "refused before it is stepped" contract.

concerns.message: Finding 6's fallback, "prove equality at the type level", cannot pass as the code stands. `duelMoveSchema.timing` is `moveTimingSchema` from `frameBudgets.ts` (outside the owned paths), which infers `active: number | "projectile-life"` and an `onBlock` union that includes `spacing-dependent`. `superRefine` doesn't narrow those. Also, `z.array` infers mutable arrays, while `duelistMoves` is declared `readonly DuelMove[]`.
concerns.consequence: `z.infer<typeof duelMoveSchema>` isn't assignable to what step.ts reads (`startup + active` stops typechecking), so the worker spends time on it or edits `frameBudgets.ts` out of bounds. It can be done inside the owned paths: intersect `moveTimingSchema` with a loose `{ active: z.int(), onBlock: frames|unguardable }` schema, and use `.readonly()` on the arrays.

concerns.message: The chord conversion doesn't say where the converted throw's startup counts from. It could keep the light's or heavy's `actionFrame`, so the throw is active 12 frames after the first press, only 10 after K when K comes 2 frames later. Or it could restart at frame 1 when the partner button arrives, so the throw is 12 frames from the completing press. The plan also doesn't say whether the window constant goes in `DuelRules` (move data, covered by the derived version) or in step.ts code (not covered).
concerns.consequence: The two choices give different replays and different frame-advantage and throw-timing tests, and reviewers can reasonably object to either one if it isn't documented. A window kept only in code isn't covered by the moveset version, so later tuning would change replay results under the same version. Recommend putting it in `DuelRules` and documenting the counting rule in `docs/duel.md`.

concerns.message: Finding 3's tie-break by previous x or velocity still needs a last resort. When the two fighters are identical in everything except slot, no slot-neutral rule can choose which one goes left. Keeping "slot 0 goes left" is in fact consistent under the test's swap-slots-and-mirror transform. It's today's use of `facing` (step.ts:417) that breaks it when both fighters face the same way. `separate()` also receives only the moved fighters, so the start-of-frame x has to be passed in.
concerns.consequence: A worker told to never reference the slot can spend a long time on a case that can't be solved. They may also ship a fallback such as not separating at all, which leaves the pushboxes overlapping and breaks the invariant that they never overlap. Agree on the fallback: previous x, then vx, then no separation that frame or the slot. Also build the exact-tie symmetry case from a hand-made state, since steering a traced run onto an exact sub-pixel tie is fragile.

concerns.message: With the current data, the guard-break cap (finding 9) never binds: a break happens only when cost > stamina, and cost ≤ 25, so stamina + 30 ≤ 54 < 100. Separately, the 3,600-frame determinism test asserts the exact set of event kinds `["block","grab","hit","throw"]` with `toEqual` (determinism.test.ts:71). After findings 1 and 2 let more throws land, `throw-clash`, `throw-escape` or `guard-break` can appear in that set.
concerns.consequence: Testing "capped at the maximum" needs a custom moveset or a hand-built state, otherwise the test only covers the uncapped branch. The event-set assertion is likely to fail for a benign reason, and it has to be updated on purpose rather than by weakening the check.

concerns.message: Finding 10's line numbers (schema.ts 923–927) don't match: the opening-reach check is at schema.ts:283–287. The fix should add `advance × (startup + active)` to each move's reach. That's conservative, because detection reads start-of-frame positions.
concerns.consequence: Only a small loss of time finding the code. The advancing thrust (64 × 18 = 1,152 sub-pixels plus a 76 px reach) still passes at the 192 px start gap, so the fixed validator shouldn't reject the current data.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Handle the throw chord without adding any state field. In the `!canAct` branch of step 4, convert when all of these hold: the fighter is attacking; its `moveId` is one of `commands.light`, `downLight`, `heavy`, `downHeavy` or `forwardHeavy`; its start-of-frame `actionFrame` ≤ the chord window (a `DuelRules` field); and the partner button's buffer is > 0. Then start `commands.throw` and consume both buttons. Every attack is started by `choose()` on a free frame, so `moveId` plus `actionFrame` already identify a move that a free fighter just started. `FighterState`, the snapshot validator and the symmetry transform don't change. For finding 2, cancel a grab only when `contacts[other]` is a hit or a block, and delete `strikeActive`. For the version, put a `movesetVersion(moveset)` function in `content/moves` (a local canonical FNV over the moveset without its `version` field), export `MOVESET_VERSION = movesetVersion(duelistMoveset)`, and have the simulation compare `movesetVersion(config.moveset)`, cached in a WeakMap, instead of trusting a stored field. For finding 5, write the validation by hand in `duel/snapshot.ts`, with no zod in `simulation`.
challenge.cheap_experiment: In a scratch vitest file, build `changed = { ...duelistMoveset, rules: { ...duelistMoveset.rules, maxHealth: 999 } }`. Check that `restoreDuel({ moveset: changed }, snapshotDuel(createDuelState(defaultDuelConfig)))` currently succeeds, which confirms the stored-field trap. Time `hashState(duelistMoveset)` over 3,600 calls. In the same file, try `expectTypeOf<z.infer<typeof duelMoveSchema>>().toEqualTypeOf<DuelMove>()`. It takes about five minutes and settles two choices before any code is written: whether the version must be computed from `config.moveset` with a cache instead of trusted as a field, and whether finding 6 needs a narrowed timing schema.

duel.task:
# Task: duel

## Goal

Fix what the review of run duel-core-001 found in the duel simulation on this branch: a keyboard player must be able to throw, a strike that misses must not cancel a throw, and the rollback contract must be airtight (slot-neutral separation, a moveset version derived from the data, fully validated snapshots). Everything else about the duel stays as it is.

## Context

- This branch contains duel-core-001's result. `features/duel-core/duel-task.md` and `features/duel-core/decisions.md` still define the duel, and all of it still applies. Read `docs/duel.md` first, then `packages/simulation/src/duel/step.ts`, `snapshot.ts`, `replay.ts` and `packages/content/src/moves`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`; the packages' `postbuild` self-checks must keep passing.
- The `world-sea` feature may still be running on the rest of the repository. Stay inside your owned paths.

Findings to fix (P1 are required):

1. (P1) Throw input. `step.ts` starts a jab as soon as `light` is buffered alone (around line 369), so pressing J and then K one or two frames later gives a jab, never a throw. Keyboard rollover rarely lands both keys on the same 60 Hz frame. Add a short throw chord window (one or two frames, a named rule constant): a light or heavy that a free fighter started converts into a throw when its partner button arrives within the window, before the move's first active frame. Prefer this conversion because it keeps every §8 startup (the jab stays 7 frames from the press). Delaying a lone light or heavy instead is acceptable only if the task's frame-advantage and punish tests still hold and `docs/duel.md` states the added delay.
2. (P1) Whiff beats throw. The throw-cancel check (around lines 73–74) uses `strikeActive`, which is true "whether or not it reaches". A jab facing away or out of range therefore cancels a connecting throw. Cancel a throw only when the opponent's strike actually hits or is blocked on that frame.
3. (P2) `separate()` breaks an exact tie (equal x and equal facing) by slot, so a mirrored run can differ. Break it without reference to the slot (for example by previous x or velocity), and cover it with the symmetry test.
4. (P2) `MOVESET_VERSION` is the hand-written string `"duelist-1"`. Derive the version that snapshots and replays carry from the move data itself (for example `hashState` of the moveset), so changed data can never keep an old version.
5. (P2) `restoreDuel` checks only the top-level shape. Validate every field of a restored state (types, integer ranges, known move ids, both fighters) before it is stepped, and refuse anything else.
6. (P2) `DuelMove` and `DuelMoveset` are hand-written beside their zod schemas and joined with `as` casts. Derive the types with `z.infer` (or prove equality at the type level). Replace the three `as unknown as Pair<...>` casts in `step.ts` with a typed helper.
7. (P2) The symmetry test doesn't assert that its scripted trade happens. Assert that the same-frame jab trade gives both fighters a hit event.
8. (P2) `docs/duel.md` doesn't mention the counter slash's strike invulnerability or the throw chord window. Add both.

Found by the official reviewers of duel-core-001 (general and coverage):

9. (P2) A guard break sets stamina to 30 (`step.ts`, around line 289: `Math.min(maxStamina, guardBreakStaminaRestore)`). §7 says a guard break "restores 30 stamina": add 30, capped at the maximum.
10. (P2) The moveset validator's "no free opening hit" check (`packages/content/src/moves/schema.ts`, around lines 923–927) ignores a move's `advance`, so an advancing special could reach an opponent at the start distance. Include the distance a move travels through startup and active frames.
11. (P2) The guard-break test (`duel.test.ts`, around line 327) probes only the cost threshold from a fresh state. Also cover a guard break after regeneration timing matters, and the stamina restored by a break.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Change only what these findings need, keep the existing structure, names and patterns, and keep every existing test passing unless a finding says it is wrong.
- Pure, integer, deterministic, as before. No new dependencies.
- Changing input timing (finding 1) changes replays. Update the recorded determinism fixtures and hash pins deliberately, and say so in `docs/duel.md`.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests: a guard break adds 30 stamina capped at the maximum; the opening-hit validator rejects a moveset whose advancing special reaches from the start distance. J then K at 0, 1 and 2 frames apart from a free fighter all give a throw, and a lone J gives a jab after the chord window. An active strike facing away or out of range doesn't cancel a connecting throw, and one that connects still does. The exact-tie separation is slot-neutral under the mirrored symmetry test. A restored snapshot with any malformed field is refused. Changing any move datum changes the moveset version, and a snapshot or replay from the old data is refused.
- All the duel-core acceptance still holds, including determinism over 3,600 frames, rollback replay and the `postbuild` self-checks.
- `npm ci` then the four policy checks pass from a clean checkout.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After ninety minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

# Task: duel

## Goal

Fix what the review of run duel-core-001 found in the duel simulation on this branch: a keyboard player must be able to throw, a strike that misses must not cancel a throw, and the rollback contract must be airtight (slot-neutral separation, a moveset version derived from the data, fully validated snapshots). Everything else about the duel stays as it is.

## Context

- This branch contains duel-core-001's result. `features/duel-core/duel-task.md` and `features/duel-core/decisions.md` still define the duel, and all of it still applies. Read `docs/duel.md` first, then `packages/simulation/src/duel/step.ts`, `snapshot.ts`, `replay.ts` and `packages/content/src/moves`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`; the packages' `postbuild` self-checks must keep passing.
- The `world-sea` feature may still be running on the rest of the repository. Stay inside your owned paths.

Findings to fix (P1 are required):

1. (P1) Throw input. `step.ts` starts a jab as soon as `light` is buffered alone (around line 369), so pressing J and then K one or two frames later gives a jab, never a throw. Keyboard rollover rarely lands both keys on the same 60 Hz frame. Add a short throw chord window (one or two frames, a named rule constant): a light or heavy that a free fighter started converts into a throw when its partner button arrives within the window, before the move's first active frame. Prefer this conversion because it keeps every §8 startup (the jab stays 7 frames from the press). Delaying a lone light or heavy instead is acceptable only if the task's frame-advantage and punish tests still hold and `docs/duel.md` states the added delay.
2. (P1) Whiff beats throw. The throw-cancel check (around lines 73–74) uses `strikeActive`, which is true "whether or not it reaches". A jab facing away or out of range therefore cancels a connecting throw. Cancel a throw only when the opponent's strike actually hits or is blocked on that frame.
3. (P2) `separate()` breaks an exact tie (equal x and equal facing) by slot, so a mirrored run can differ. Break it without reference to the slot (for example by previous x or velocity), and cover it with the symmetry test.
4. (P2) `MOVESET_VERSION` is the hand-written string `"duelist-1"`. Derive the version that snapshots and replays carry from the move data itself (for example `hashState` of the moveset), so changed data can never keep an old version.
5. (P2) `restoreDuel` checks only the top-level shape. Validate every field of a restored state (types, integer ranges, known move ids, both fighters) before it is stepped, and refuse anything else.
6. (P2) `DuelMove` and `DuelMoveset` are hand-written beside their zod schemas and joined with `as` casts. Derive the types with `z.infer` (or prove equality at the type level). Replace the three `as unknown as Pair<...>` casts in `step.ts` with a typed helper.
7. (P2) The symmetry test doesn't assert that its scripted trade happens. Assert that the same-frame jab trade gives both fighters a hit event.
8. (P2) `docs/duel.md` doesn't mention the counter slash's strike invulnerability or the throw chord window. Add both.

Found by the official reviewers of duel-core-001 (general and coverage):

9. (P2) A guard break sets stamina to 30 (`step.ts`, around line 289: `Math.min(maxStamina, guardBreakStaminaRestore)`). §7 says a guard break "restores 30 stamina": add 30, capped at the maximum.
10. (P2) The moveset validator's "no free opening hit" check (`packages/content/src/moves/schema.ts`, around lines 923–927) ignores a move's `advance`, so an advancing special could reach an opponent at the start distance. Include the distance a move travels through startup and active frames.
11. (P2) The guard-break test (`duel.test.ts`, around line 327) probes only the cost threshold from a fresh state. Also cover a guard break after regeneration timing matters, and the stamina restored by a break.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Change only what these findings need, keep the existing structure, names and patterns, and keep every existing test passing unless a finding says it is wrong.
- Pure, integer, deterministic, as before. No new dependencies.
- Changing input timing (finding 1) changes replays. Update the recorded determinism fixtures and hash pins deliberately, and say so in `docs/duel.md`.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests: a guard break adds 30 stamina capped at the maximum; the opening-hit validator rejects a moveset whose advancing special reaches from the start distance. J then K at 0, 1 and 2 frames apart from a free fighter all give a throw, and a lone J gives a jab after the chord window. An active strike facing away or out of range doesn't cancel a connecting throw, and one that connects still does. The exact-tie separation is slot-neutral under the mirrored symmetry test. A restored snapshot with any malformed field is refused. Changing any move datum changes the moveset version, and a snapshot or replay from the old data is refused.
- All the duel-core acceptance still holds, including determinism over 3,600 frames, rollback replay and the `postbuild` self-checks.
- `npm ci` then the four policy checks pass from a clean checkout.
